overview.business_model: The company manufactures and supplies advanced railway electronics and electro-mechanical products to Indian Railways and executes turnkey 25 kV AC railway electrification (OHE) projects. Revenue is earned across three divisions: (i) Electronics - Electronic Rectifier-cum-Regulating Units (ERRU), Vigilance Control Devices (VCD), regulated battery chargers, GPS-based passenger information systems (PAPIS) and emergency light units; (ii) Rotating Machines - brushless alternators, traction motors, oil-cooling units and armature/field coils; and (iii) Contracts - turnkey railway electrification (design, supply, erection, testing and commissioning of 25 kV AC OHE and traction substations). It operates on a largely business-to-government (B2G) model, selling primarily to Indian Railways, its production units and railway PSUs against tenders.

financial_valuation.evidence: Standalone: Operating CF (1,146.02)/(827.99)/(162.31) lakh for FY26/FY25/FY24; Investing CF (59.84)/(26.49)/23.92 lakh; Financing CF 1,209.03/876.22/142.93 lakh. Consolidated: Operating CF (1,109.55)/(965.40)/(147.48) lakh; Investing CF (59.65)/(26.45)/10.15 lakh; Financing CF 1,155.45/1,023.17/151.21 lakh (FY26/FY25/FY24 respectively).
financial_valuation.title: Negative cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities

internal_operational.detail: Business is substantially dependent on contracts from Indian Railways, zonal railways, PSUs and other Ministry of Railways-affiliated entities (GoI Entities). Any reduction in railway sector spending, adverse procurement policy changes, tender delays/cancellations, or inability to maintain historical business levels with Indian Railways could materially affect operations.
internal_operational.evidence: Government revenue was 82.01% of consolidated revenue from operations in FY26 (Rs.11,730.61 lakh), 81.50% in FY25 (Rs.9,933.16 lakh) and 67.74% in FY24 (Rs.6,722.83 lakh); standalone basis 81.50%/81.77%/68.04% for FY26/FY25/FY24 respectively.
internal_operational.title: Heavy dependence on Ministry of Railways / GoI Entities contracts

internal_operational.detail: A significant portion of revenue is derived from a limited number of clients, increasing volatility and exposure to individual contract/dispute risk; no past instance of losses from client loss disclosed.
internal_operational.evidence: Consolidated: Top 1 customer 16.09% (FY26)/30.80% (FY25)/25.36% (FY24) of revenue from operations; Top 5 customers 40.55%/53.50%/46.81%; Top 10 customers 50.38%/63.15%/55.58%. Standalone Top 10 customers 52.95%/66.62%/63.57%.
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration risk

internal_operational.detail: Company depends on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials, though reliance on top-10 suppliers has reduced as of March 31, 2026; no long-term supply agreements exist and no past disputes/losses have occurred.
internal_operational.evidence: Consolidated: Top 1 supplier 14.78% of purchases (FY26) vs 34.62% (FY25) and 31.00% (FY24); Top 5 suppliers 43.21%/49.61%/49.62%; Top 10 suppliers 52.59%/58.25%/59.20%.
internal_operational.title: Supplier concentration risk for raw materials

strategy_growth.detail: Company faces competition from domestic and multinational players in a sector where government contracts are typically awarded via competitive bidding, often to the lowest bidder; smaller/new entrants offering lower margins, or competitors adopting new technology faster, could pressure business, financial performance and market position.
strategy_growth.evidence: Contracts largely awarded under prevailing procurement policy to the lowest bidder among technically qualified bidders.
strategy_growth.title: Highly competitive industry with pressure on margins

strategy_growth.detail: Projects are generally secured through competitive bidding subject to technical/financial pre-qualification; no guarantee of meeting qualification criteria or winning bids, and JV-based bidding introduces risk from partner negligence/disqualification, potentially limiting operational flexibility and affecting business, prospects and financial condition.
strategy_growth.evidence: As of the RHP date, the company has not participated in any tender process through collaboration/JV with another entity.
strategy_growth.title: Dependence on pre-qualification and competitive tendering for new projects

strategy_growth.detail: Tendering by the Ministry of Railways and affiliated entities is complex, structured and time-consuming with stringent eligibility criteria and multi-stage evaluation; delays, deferment, modification, cancellation, re-invitation of tenders, or bid rejection despite technical qualification could adversely affect order inflows, project schedules and revenue recognition, while raising bid-preparation costs.
strategy_growth.evidence: General process-risk disclosure without company-specific quantified past instance.
strategy_growth.title: Complex and time-consuming Ministry of Railways tendering processes

concerns_observed: Extremely high customer concentration risk with 81.50% of standalone FY2026 revenue from Government entities, primarily Ministry of Railways; top 10 customers account for 52.95%.
Significant geographical concentration: 59.01% of FY2026 revenue from Uttarakhand and 49.28% of raw material procurement from Delhi, exposing operations to regional disruptions.

Persistent negative operating cash flows for three consecutive years (FY2024: Rs.(162.31) Lakhs, FY2025: Rs.(827.99) Lakhs, FY2026: Rs.(1,146.02) Lakhs standalone) driven by rising trade receivables and working capital needs.
Escalating working capital requirements (FY2026: Rs.11,896.73 Lakhs) and borrowings (FY2026: Rs.6,331.88 Lakhs) with high finance costs (FY2026: Rs.792.53 Lakhs), straining profitability.
Multiple instances of delayed statutory filings under GST, TDS, EPF, ESI, and Companies Act, attributed to internal control weaknesses and absence of dedicated compliance officer.
Clerical error in PAS-3 filing with adjudication pending; incorrect disclosure of allotment price and consideration type.

Extensive related party transactions including unsecured loans from promoters repayable on demand (total outstanding Rs.1,524.95 Lakhs in FY2026), sales/purchases with promoter group entities, and sub-leased factory premises from related parties.

Outstanding legal proceedings: Company faces claims of Rs.1,593.54 Lakhs (including Rs.1,361.37 Lakhs criminal proceedings against the Company); contingent liabilities of Rs.4,887.49 Lakhs as of March 31, 2026.
No prior public market for equity shares; issue price discovery via book building may not reflect post-listing market price; liquidity risk.
Post-issue promoter and promoter group will hold 60.94%, enabling significant control over shareholder matters.
Some directors lack experience with listed companies, posing governance and compliance risks.
No monitoring agency appointed for issue proceeds utilization; deployment at management and board discretion.
No dividend payment history; working capital intensive business may limit future dividend capacity.
Current promoters are not original promoters; transition may raise concerns about legacy decisions and continuity.

parameter_scores.basis: Standalone FY2026 revenue from Government: 81.50% (Rs.11,730.60 Lakhs). Top 1 customer: 15.99%; Top 5: 40.36%; Top 10: 52.95%. Geographical concentration: Uttarakhand 59.01%. Heavy dependence on Ministry of Railways and competitive L1 bidding.

PAT not disclosed in extracted P&L. Negative operating cash flows for three years: FY2024 Rs.(162.31) Lakhs, FY2025 Rs.(827.99) Lakhs, FY2026 Rs.(1,146.02) Lakhs standalone. Finance costs rising: FY2024 Rs.696.10 Lakhs, FY2025 Rs.686.18 Lakhs, FY2026 Rs.792.53 Lakhs.

Working capital requirement FY2026: Rs.11,896.73 Lakhs; borrowings FY2026: Rs.6,331.88 Lakhs. Total outstanding secured borrowings Rs.4,383.78 Lakhs, unsecured Rs.3,030.43 Lakhs (standalone). Unsecured promoter loans Rs.1,524.95 Lakhs repayable on demand. Interest rates up to 26.77% on some borrowings.

Multiple delayed GST, TDS, EPF, ESI filings across FY2020-2026. Delayed Companies Act filings including AOC-4, MGT-7, DPT-3, ADT-1, MSME, DIR-12, MGT-14, CHG-1, PAS-6, CRA-2. Clerical error in PAS-3 with pending adjudication. No committee composition disclosed. Some directors lack listed company experience.

Total litigation amount: Rs.2,540.47 Lakhs (Company Rs.1,593.54 Lakhs including Rs.1,361.37 Lakhs criminal proceedings). Contingent liabilities: Rs.4,887.49 Lakhs (claims not acknowledged Rs.1,153.12 Lakhs + guarantees/LC Rs.3,734.37 Lakhs as of March 31, 2026).

Promoter holding 73.50% pre-issue; zero pledging. However, extensive RPTs: FY2026 sales to Safe System India Rs.805.63 Lakhs (5.60%), purchases from Safe Insulation Technologies Rs.765.54 Lakhs (5.32%), unsecured loans from promoters/directors Rs.1,524.95 Lakhs outstanding. Sub-leased factories from related party Safe System India. Promoter avg cost Rs.3.33-11.86 vs potential issue price.

Niche railway electrification and component manufacturing with ISO 9001:2015. Order book Rs.18,105.44 Lakhs as of May 31, 2026. However, entirely dependent on government tendering (L1 system), no long-term supply agreements, limited brand visibility outside government sector, pending trademark registration.

Objects: Rs.3,360 Lakhs for working capital (FY2027 projected). No capex or capacity expansion. No appraisal by bank/financial institution. No monitoring agency appointed. No alternative funding identified. General corporate purposes amount unspecified.

red_flags: Persistent negative operating cash flows for three consecutive years despite revenue growth, indicating severe working capital strain and potential cash conversion issues.
Extremely high customer concentration with >81% revenue from Government/Railways, combined with L1 bidding system, creating existential dependency on a single client type.
Multiple statutory filing delays across GST, TDS, EPF, ESI, and Companies Act spanning several years, with self-attributed internal control weaknesses — governance red flag.
Clerical error in PAS-3 filing (incorrect allotment price and consideration type) with pending adjudication — indicates poor financial controls and potential regulatory penalties.
Outstanding criminal proceedings against the Company amounting to Rs.1,361.37 Lakhs — nature undisclosed, materiality high.

Extensive related party transactions including unsecured promoter loans repayable on demand (Rs.1,524.95 Lakhs), sub-leased factories from promoter group entities, and significant inter-company sales/purchases — conflict of interest and financial entanglement risks.
No monitoring agency for issue proceeds; deployment entirely at management discretion for working capital — no external validation of fund requirement.
Some directors lack listed company experience; board committee composition not disclosed — governance risk for a soon-to-be-listed entity.
Current promoters are not original promoters; transition history and legacy liabilities unclear.
strengths_observed: Established track record with over 18 years of operations since incorporation in 2005, serving Ministry of Railways and affiliated entities.
Diversified product portfolio across Electronics, Rotating Machines, and Contracts divisions, covering critical railway components and turnkey electrification projects.
Consistent revenue growth: FY2024 Rs.9,921.78 Lakhs, FY2025 Rs.12,148.16 Lakhs, FY2026 Rs.14,392.78 Lakhs (standalone).
Strong order book visibility with unexecuted orders of Rs.18,105.44 Lakhs as of May 31, 2026, providing near-term revenue pipeline.
ISO 9001:2015 certification indicating quality management systems in place.
Promoter holding at 73.50% pre-issue with zero pledging on promoter shares, signaling alignment and no leverage risk on promoter equity.
No history of blacklisting, debarment, or suspension by government authorities in the past three financial years.
Experienced management team with promoters and directors possessing over 30 years in the electrical industry, including specialized power electronics expertise (IIT Madras).

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
sk.schemes: SECI wind auctions (Tranche-XVII)|GUVNL state wind auctions (Phase X)|Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme|Make in India|Semiconductor initiatives
sk.structure: DG sets classified by capacity: LHP (7.5-160 kVA), MHP (180-500 kVA), HHP (>500 kVA); MSLG sets 3-10 MW for continuous/base-load. Wind potential concentrated in five states: Rajasthan (24%), Gujarat (16%), Maharashtra (15%), Karnataka (15%), Andhra Pradesh (11%).

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company procures raw materials and components, undertakes in-house manufacturing and value-addition processes, and supplies finished or value-added products to its customers; the Contract Division separately undertakes execution of turnkey electrification contracts (design, supply, erection, testing and commissioning) forming part of the Company's service operations. Manufacturing follows an in-house sequence from Bill of Materials presentation through vendor-sourced procurement, incoming quality check, stage-wise assembly/testing, to final dispatch after mandatory Third-Party Inspection (TPI) by Indian Railways.

commitments.body:

- **Company believes listing on the Emerge Platform of NSE will enhance its corporate image, brand name and create a public market for its Equity Shares in India.**
- **Company's stated vision is to strive to be best in its class by offering state-of-the-art products with regard to standard of workmanship, secure working procedures, practices and policies.**
